For 3s orbital of hydrogen atom, the normalised wave function is given by\par
$\psi_{3s}=\dfrac{1}{81\sqrt{3\pi}}\left(\dfrac1{a_0}\right)^{3/2}\left[27-\dfrac{18r}{a_0}+\dfrac{2r^2}{a_0^2}\right]e^{-\frac r{3a_0}}$\par

\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA09-P2-CHEM-S1-Q07, source={Score Advanced - Test 09 (29 Apr 2023)}, paper=2, qno=7, type=multi, subtopic={Orbitals}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S1 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: probability density of an s orbital electron, orbitals | steps: spherical symmetry; radial probability}]
The nucleus of an atom is located at x = y = z = 0. If the probability of finding an `s' orbital electron in a tiny volume around x = a, y = z = 0 is 1.0 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$. Choose the correct statement(s) regarding the probability of finding electron.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The probability of finding the electron in the same-sized volume around x = z = 0, y = a is the same i.e., 1 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$}
\opt{B}{The probability of finding the electron in the same-sized volume around x = y = 0, z = a is zero}
\opt{C}{The probability of finding the electron at x = y = z = 0 is zero.}
\opt{D}{The probability of finding the electron at x = 2a, y = z = 0 must be greater than 1.0 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA10-P1-CHEM-S1-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 10 (06 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=multi, subtopic={Orbitals}, answer={B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=9, diff_parts={K3 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: statements on hydrogenic radial wave functions, orbitals, node counting | steps: node counting; the radial probability maximum for 1s; the radial node of 2s}]
(i) $\psi_r = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{a_0}\right)^{3/2} e^{-r/na_0}$\par
(ii) $\psi_r = \dfrac{1}{9\sqrt{3}}\left(\dfrac{1}{a_0}\right)^{3/2}(6 - 6\sigma + \sigma^2)e^{-\sigma/2}$\par
(iii) $\psi_r = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{a_0}\right)^{3/2}\left(2 - \dfrac{2r}{na_0}\right)e^{-r/na_0}$\par
(iv) $\psi_r = \dfrac{1}{9\sqrt{6}}\left(\dfrac{1}{a_0}\right)^{3/2}(4 - \sigma)\sigma e^{-\sigma/2}$, where $\sigma = \dfrac{2r}{na_0}$\par
Based on above radial functions for different orbitals, select correct statement(s) :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{for orbital (iv), the graph between $\psi_r$ and r will intersect x axis at two distinct non-zero finite values of r.}
\opt{B}{for orbital (i), the radial probability of finding electron will be maximum at r = a$_0$.}
\opt{C}{for orbital (ii), there is no angular node}
\opt{D}{for orbital (iii), distance of radial node from origin is `2a$_0$'}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
